ai_summary: Great Britain's wind generation currently stands at 10.9 GW, with Scottish wind output contributing an estimated 4.4 GW, representing 43.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exemplary carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh versus 156 gCO2/kWh GB-wide, north-south transmission bottlenecks prevent this abundant renewable power from reaching southern demand centers. As a consequence, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 76.5 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £2,113,721. To replace this displaced zero-carbon electricity, an estimated 14,536,007 m3 of gas has been burned elsewhere across the grid, emitting an additional 26,777 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing this single-day run-rate suggests a total yearly curtailment cost of approximately £772 million. When recovered through national network balancing charges, this inefficiency adds an estimated £3/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK. This persistent operational bottleneck highlights the urgent economic and environmental case for expanding cross-border transmission capacity to ensure clean Scottish power is delivered rather than turned down.
